firstUseObservations: Search was the clearest route to a known key and returned requirement, run and verification plan together.
Requirement details and acceptance criteria were understandable. Component allocation and verification-plan links made the intended support discoverable.
Verified by is an easy label to overread as success, although it led to a plan. The assessment's explanation that ordinary connections do not establish evaluated dependencies was useful.
The original run looked like a plain artifact with no direct connections and no result summary in its inspector; without working assessment, its purpose and outcome were opaque.

Assess evidence clicks timed out while inspector was open. Closing inspector allowed the action. DOM inspection helped discover the close control; no screenshots were available to assess whether the overlap was visually obvious.

Requirement creation exposed many mandatory camelCase status fields with free-text inputs and no visible allowed values or defaults. I supplied candidate/not started/not verified/not validated based on judgment. This is demanding for a first-time author.

The New item task initially rendered its heading and return control before its form appeared; later reads showed the form. Create/connect/save also needed a later observation before success appeared. No duplicate submits were made.
Save feedback, revision numbers, version history and inspected saved statement made persistence convincing. The create form stayed visible after success, which could invite duplicate creation.
Draft interruption recovery was strong: explicit unsaved notice, Resume editing and Discard edits preserved intent while navigating.

Source identity versus contextual reference remained unclear: duplicate docs/architecture.md rows shared one UUID and file paths appeared beside UUIDs with generic contextual-reference labeling. I did not inspect source content or pins. Pin semantics therefore remain untested.

Evaluation versus structural relationship was understandable from the assessment explanatory text, but the actual captures and current-applicability review could not be learned because of the read blocker.

initialReport.screenshotLimitation: Snapshot failed twice; supported CUA fallback was unavailable/timed out. No screenshot artifact was captured, so visual claims are limited.
recommendations: Fix evidence read failure and expose a stable retryable error with context; keep the historical result immutable and let applicability review be recorded once inputs load.
Show recorded outcome and evidence-read status in a result artifact inspector so a result is recognizable even when assessment cannot load.
Use explicit verification-plan wording where Verified by might imply a completed pass.
Provide readable status labels, suggested values and safe draft defaults in requirement creation; reduce mandatory bookkeeping for a draft.
Make successful creation visibly transition to the saved record or disable duplicate create submission.
Ensure inspector overlap does not silently block primary assessment actions, and verify the actual CSS viewport at 680px with functioning screenshot tooling.
Explain source identity, contextual references and pins close to their controls; distinguish repeated references to one source from duplicate source objects.

recordedOutcome.title: REQ-001 field-definition verification run
recordedOutcome.exactText: PASS — REQ-001 AC-1 and AC-2: custom required/optional string, number, boolean and JSON field definitions/values persist through reopen; invalid schemas/values/updates and mixed batches reject without partial native/evidence writes. Seven focused headless checks and five production browser checks passed. This is technical verification, not human user validation.
recordedOutcome.qualification: This is the outcome recorded by the existing run; this agent did not execute or independently validate those checks.

freshness.explanation: Nine declared contextual-reference relationships were also shown separately and matched. Input freshness and recorded outcome were explicitly labeled independent.

changedInput.uncertainty: The UI established a scoped-content hash change but its comparison did not reveal a semantic text difference. Same resource v1 does not imply unchanged observed content. Zero unknown inputs is a machine freshness classification; semantic applicability remains uncertain.

referencePinOutcomeDistinction.sourceIdentity: Resource 4250a94f-fc2b-4b5d-af1a-d3b827114aff identifies file docs/architecture.md independently of a particular content hash.

contextualReference.explanation: Strict model writes reject unsupported schema properties and report their exact path.

referencePinOutcomeDistinction.understanding: The contextual reference describes a scoped use of a source. Its pin identifies a captured observation, while the run records a technical outcome against declared captures. Neither an unchanged reference relationship nor a pin alone establishes present conformance. Freshness, historical PASS and present applicability judgment remain separate.
referencePinOutcomeDistinction.usabilityLimit: This distinction became inspectable after the fix, but pin/selector/source identity were buried in a very large JSON disclosure including the whole schema. The changed row only used a short UUID and showed {} field panes. A readable scope label, pin summary and content diff would make the same reasoning easier.

savedReview.preservationConfirmation: Review recorded. Original outcome and captured inputs are unchanged.
savedReview.rationale: Guided agent follow-up: preserve RUN-REQ001-AUDIT's original PASS as historical technical verification of REQ-001 AC-1/AC-2 (seven focused headless and five production browser checks); this is not human validation. Current applicability needs reevaluation: the declared docs/architecture.md resource 4250a94f-fc2b-4b5d-af1a-d3b827114aff has changed scoped-content hash despite captured/current resource v1 and matching contextual-reference relationships. The definition reference for Model input validation is pinned to an observation; that pin identifies captured evidence and does not prove the current content or implementation conforms. UI reports 1 changed, 0 unknown, 18 matching of 19 inputs. Captured/current field panes for the changed resource show {}, so I cannot determine the semantic effect of the change from this comparison. Compare the changed definition scope with the captured observation and reevaluate or rerun affected AC-2 checks before claiming current applicability. Do not overwrite the immutable original result.
savedReview.reloadVerification: After reload, Decision recorded, same review ID/timestamp, review rationale, Freshness changed / Review needs_reevaluation, and original recorded PASS remained visible.
savedReview.note: Review persistence did not increment the native workspace revision; the separate review ID and reload confirmation establish the recorded review.

defect.trigger: An actual evaluation explicitly declared object and relationship inputs. Production assessment received valid working-context data but rejected it in the client response validator.
defect.rootCause: validateComparison compared inputCount against object comparisons alone; compact input validation also assumed one captured version/state per identity despite separately scoped uses.
defect.resolution: Count both declaration kinds, validate aggregate known-change/unknown state across all uses, preserve a captured version only when unambiguous, and continue rejecting forged versions/hidden changes/count mismatches.
defect.crossFieldChecks: HTTP regression covers mixed native revisions plus a direct relationship, relationship-only evaluation, exact native parity, forged compact versions and hidden-change rejection.
defect.uiRegression: Production reference authoring now opens normal assessment after a relationship-input evaluation, at desktop and phone widths.

executedCriteria.acceptance: AC-1: A relationship can be declared as a current-guarded or exact historical input independent of output reachability. AC-2: Capture retains its version, qualification, endpoints and governing schema; content states require explicit declaration. AC-3: Native annotations and observed resource content can be separately scoped and compared. AC-4: Later edits/removal do not rewrite captured inputs/outcome; legacy receipts and explicit forward-path behavior remain unchanged. AC-5: Captured inputs retain explicitly declared contextual usage roles alongside their selected native/external state; a usage role does not alter resource identity or infer undeclared dependencies.
executedCriteria.scope: Additional reader regression for already specified direct-relationship/repeated-use/state semantics; other acceptance remains supported by earlier separately captured results.

executedCriteria.acceptance: AC-1: Current means latest observed/recorded state with availability/time disclosure; pinned selection never silently retargets. AC-2: Missing access or unresolved/ambiguous passage scope reports unknown while retaining known changes. AC-3: Whole-file hash drift does not claim passage change or semantic irrelevance. AC-4: Capture identifies whether content is retained/retrievable/unknown; comparison and review preserve original outcomes and keep current applicability separate.
executedCriteria.scope: Additional reader regression for already specified direct-relationship/repeated-use/state semantics; other acceptance remains supported by earlier separately captured results.

verification.history: The first focused browser regression used an outdated Return button locator and failed twice; corrected it to the actual Back to graph label. Both journeys then passed, and the full 188-test suite passed. No application behavior was changed to bypass those test failures.

remainingFindings.proposedScope: Present the existing resource label/identity, native annotation version, selected/latest observed state and reference scope clearly; preserve unknown semantic relevance and immutable outcomes. No new primitive or automatic passage interpretation is implied.
